audit.why: Chart reads Akshan, Skill, Singed, Singed, Akshan, Singed, Singed on both layers and matches audits/top/akshan__singed.json, which examined it and left it. The singed packet says it contradicts a 53.73% win rate; the mirror wins the tie.
audit.corrected: Left as-is, flagged to the user.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears anywhere, and level 6 is framed purely as 'pop Insanity Potion before crossing open ground'.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and only 12s maxed — the longest escape cooldown in the lane and the real window to attack. Comeuppance is 100s. Avengerang is 9s at rank 1 falling to 5s. Mega Adhesive 17s, Fling 10s, Insanity Potion 100s.
audit.corrected: 18s Heroic Swing, 100s Comeuppance, 9s Avengerang and Singed's own timers written into the cooldown row, spikes, whys, early and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is absent: Mega Adhesive GROUNDS, and Heroic Swing is a grapple-swing, so grounded he cannot cast it at all. Instead the entry says he 'kites your W throw with Heroic Swing' and tells you to save the goo for chokepoints. Comeuppance is also described as an unavoidable snipe when Riot's text stops it on the first champion, minion or structure hit — a minion body-blocks it. And wants.foe[1] says the grapple 'denies the root'; the root only exists when Fling lands a target inside the adhesive.
audit.why: Singed W: 'slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it'. Akshan E: 'fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it'. Akshan R: 'dealing damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit'.
audit.corrected: Grounding of Heroic Swing, the minion body-block on Comeuppance, and the real Fling-into-adhesive root are all stated now.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Akshan's passive camouflage' at level 1, and 'Heroic Swing's cooldown shortens on his passive camouflage resets'.
audit.why: His passive is Dirty Fighting — a third-hit shield plus an extra attack. Camouflage is Going Rogue (W), it only runs while he moves toward Scoundrels, and it drops fast away from brush or terrain. Nothing in his kit refreshes Heroic Swing from camouflage. Two invented mechanics in a row teach the reader to fear the wrong thing.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Dirty Fighting's third-hit shield and the real Going Rogue conditions.

edits.before: Weather the poke — poison-kite him and fling the Heroic Swing commit. Singed wins the Heroic Swing cooldown windows.
edits.after: Weather the poke — Mega Adhesive grounds Heroic Swing, so a glued Akshan cannot grapple out of your poison at all.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Akshan Heroic Swing (18s at rank 1): his only escape, and Mega Adhesive grounds it outright. - Comeuppance (100s): a minion body-blocks it. - Avengerang (9s): the poke you eat. - Your Fling: 10s. - Insanity Potion: kill windows.

edits.before: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and needs terrain — grounded in the goo it will not cast.

edits.before: You lose most level-1 duels — set up the proxy game instead. Identify how Akshan contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: You lose the level-1 poke war — hug your minions so Avengerang splits its damage, and let him push the wave into you instead.

edits.before: Ult-ghost-proxy is a macro weapon — you win by farming where he is not. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Akshan's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Comeuppance (100s) reads your missing health but stops on the first body it hits — keep a minion between you and his firing line.

edits.before: Track Akshan's Heroic Swing: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. When it is down — Fling into goo, poison out.
edits.after: Track Heroic Swing (18s at rank 1): it needs terrain to anchor, and Mega Adhesive grounds it — glued, he has no exit.

edits.before: Akshan's Avengerang poke and passive camouflage make the first wave a genuine coin-flip — stand near minions, not in open lane, to minimize free hits.
edits.after: Avengerang (9s at rank 1) out-ranges everything you own, and Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit — stand in your minions, not the open lane.

edits.before: Akshan's Comeuppance gives him a long-range snipe that punishes you running in the open — pop Insanity Potion BEFORE crossing open ground, not after you're already taking damage.
edits.after: Comeuppance (100s) reads your missing health but stops on the first champion, minion or structure — keep a minion on the line rather than trusting Insanity Potion to eat it.

edits.before: Herd Akshan into a wall or your W goo with Fling, then run past and let Poison Trail do the work as he chases
edits.after: Glue his feet with Mega Adhesive — grounded, Heroic Swing will not fire, then Fling him back into it to root

edits.before: Use Heroic Swing's grapple to stay mobile and dodge your Mega Adhesive throw, denying the root
edits.after: Grapple out on Heroic Swing before the goo lands — once grounded, the swing does not cast at all

edits.before: Bait you into walking under his tower by feigning low HP, then Comeuppance snipes you while you over-commit
edits.after: Feign low HP to draw you under tower, then Comeuppance you through a gap where no minion blocks the line

edits.before: Akshan's Avengerang poke reaches you before your Poison Trail reaches him — stay near your minions to split the damage, and do not blow Flash chasing a camouflaged target you cannot see.
edits.after: Avengerang (9s at rank 1) reaches you before Poison Trail reaches him, and Dirty Fighting shields his third hit — stand in your minions to split the boomerang and give him nothing to punish.

edits.before: His Heroic Swing gives him instant repositioning that beats your level-2 run-at-you pattern — only Fling if he has already used the grapple on terrain and is on foot.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and needs terrain to anchor — that is your window, not his. Step up while the swing is down and he has nothing left but move speed.

edits.before: Full kit online but he still kites your W throw with Heroic Swing — save Mega Adhesive for terrain chokepoints where his grapple anchor is blocked.
edits.after: Full kit online: Mega Adhesive grounds him, and grounded there is no grapple — glue his feet, then Fling him back into the goo to root him.

edits.before: Comeuppance snipe punishes you running in the open — hug terrain and pop Insanity Potion before crossing open ground so the stat dump eats the damage rather than your base HP.
edits.after: Comeuppance (100s) scales with your missing health but stops on the first body it hits — hug terrain, keep a minion in the line, and never stand clear in the open.

edits.before: Heroic Swing's cooldown shortens on his passive camouflage resets, so he still has an escape answer even after you complete Rylai's — bait the dash first, then commit the Fling-into-goo combo.
edits.after: Going Rogue's camouflage only runs while he moves at a Scoundrel and dies away from terrain — it does not refresh Heroic Swing, so once the 18s swing is spent he is on foot.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are largely his — Akshan's Avengerang poke costs you HP before you can even set up a run-past, and his passive camouflage makes it hard to track when he is repositioning for a bigger engage. Don't try to run at him yet; last-hit with Poison Trail from close to your own minions and accept that you are in a survival window. At level 3 your Mega Adhesive root combo comes online, which is your first real threat — if he ever steps past the wave to poke, W the ground behind him and Fling him toward your tower. The poison does the rest if he panics and walks back through the cloud, but only punish a clear mistake, not a guessed position.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are largely his — Avengerang (9s at rank 1) costs you HP before you can set up a run-past, and Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit, so your chip does less than the bar suggests. Don't run at him yet; last-hit with Poison Trail from inside your own minions and accept a survival window. At level 3 the real threat arrives: Mega Adhesive grounds, and Heroic Swing is a grapple, so a man standing in your goo cannot swing anywhere. If he steps past the wave to poke, glue his feet and Fling him back into the adhesive — landing in it roots him and the poison does the rest. Punish a clear mistake, not a guessed position.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 he still owns the poke war, but you switch to proxy mode to rob him of the value of that advantage. Shove the wave fast into his tower, then loop behind it — his Heroic Swing mobility lets him follow, but following a Singed into a tight corridor is exactly what you want. Pop Insanity Potion when he commits to an all-in or when you need to run a full poison loop; the stat dump buys you enough durability to survive a burst sequence he was planning on killing you with. His level-6 Comeuppance snipe is the main new threat — stay near terrain so he cannot draw a clean line, and never stand still in the open when the cast animation starts.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 he still owns the poke war, so switch to proxy mode and rob it of value. Shove fast into his tower, then loop behind it — Heroic Swing lets him follow, but following a Singed into a tight corridor is exactly what you want, because the glue grounds the swing and he needs terrain to anchor it in the first place. Pop Insanity Potion (100s) when he commits, not to tank poke: the stats buy you the seconds his burst needed. His level-6 Comeuppance is the new threat and it stops on the first body in the line — stay near terrain, keep a minion between you, and never stand clear in the open when the channel starts.

notes: Two invented mechanics removed: a level-1 'passive camouflage' (his passive is Dirty Fighting; camouflage is Going Rogue, W) and 'Heroic Swing's cooldown shortens on his passive camouflage resets' — no such refresh exists. Both taught the reader to fear the wrong ability. The matchup-deciding fact, that Mega Adhesive grounds and a grounded Akshan cannot cast a grapple-swing, was absent from both layers. Level chart left alone per the mirror; see questionsForUser.
